findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the Testing/Approach 'fix the CLASS + RED->GREEN reproduction passes after fix' commitment with the delivered instrumentation-only outcome: either add an AC stating that the fix is deferred until the forensics pin the deleter (and that the underlying failure may still recur), or scope the ticket's end-state explicitly to 'instrumentation to diagnose next occurrence' rather than 'fix'.
evidence: Approach: 'Then fix the CLASS (e.g., scrub GIT_* env in the fixture's _git via env= allowlist, or disable autoDetach maintenance in the fixture repo), with a regression test proving the mechanism.'
Testing: 'RED->GREEN: the reproduction fails before the fix, passes after.'
AC1: 'The organic deleter was not identified after 210 local fixture instantiations under xdist plus ~29,400 prior green executions, so the sanctioned instrumentation path below applies.'
AC2 delivers forensics capture in _GitFailed, not a behavioral fix to the fixture.
Context: 'it will keep blocking UNRELATED changes' Verified votes at random'.
findings.finding: The Testing section commits to a RED->GREEN cycle where 'the reproduction fails before the fix, passes after' and 'The fix must not weaken what the fixture proves', and the Approach says 'Then fix the CLASS ... with a regression test proving the mechanism' — but the Acceptance Criteria (all marked done) deliver only failure-time forensics instrumentation in _GitFailed, with the organic deleter explicitly 'not identified' and no fix that turns a reproduction green. The plan's own stated end-state (fix the integrity fault so it stops 'blocking UNRELATED changes' Verified votes at random') is not reached; the closed ticket delivers a diagnostic that only pins the mechanism on the NEXT CI occurrence.
findings.location: Testing section ('RED->GREEN: the reproduction fails before the fix, passes after') vs Acceptance Criteria AC1/AC2
findings.suggested_fix: Revise the Testing section to reflect the not-reproducible branch actually taken (forensics-first, fix deferred) and add an explicit AC acknowledging the underlying object-store fault remains unfixed pending the next CI capture, so the closed state matches the delivered work.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a candidate hypothesis for the transient git-read path: build_ticket_position_commit_map fails closed to {} on rc!=0/empty-stdout/EAGAIN (per its own docstring, src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:331-332) and the fixture treats one raw call as guaranteed non-empty — test this class BEFORE concluding the mechanism is object-store deletion.
evidence: Plan: candidate hypotheses (a) env leakage (b) detached maintenance (c) global git config (d) tmp_path collision — all object-store-directed
src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:331-332 'Never raises: ANY git failure yields {} and the caller falls back to the per-event resolver' — a transient fail-closed path present in-source the whole time

Third-recurrence RCA (ticket comment): 'deleting the 1005 loose blob left BOTH broad and narrow history walks healthy ... refuting the prior ENOENT class'; injected rc128/empty/EAGAIN each reproduced the organic batched-empty sequence
findings.finding: The plan's hypothesis set (a)-(d) is exhaustively framed around object-store deletion/integrity and never enumerates the mechanism that actually produced the flake: the fixture depends on the fail-closed optimization helper build_ticket_position_commit_map returning a non-empty map on its first attempt, though its documented contract returns {} on ANY transient git failure and production callers fall back per-event. The 'byte-for-byte reproduction' was achieved by artificial loose-object deletion, which does not match the organic transient-read mechanism.
findings.location: Approach section, hypotheses (a)-(d); AC line 1 ('mechanism CLASS ... proven by direct injection')
scenarios: A transient broad-git-log read (rc!=0, empty stdout, or EAGAIN under CI load) returns {} on the first attempt; the fixture asserts on it and ERRORs even though an immediate replay would succeed
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the hypothesis list with '(e) the fixture asserts directly on a fail-closed optimization helper (build_ticket_position_commit_map) that returns {} on any transient git read', and inject a first-attempt rc128/empty/EAGAIN at the subprocess boundary to test it, since the source contract already documents that failure mode.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pair the instrumentation with a defensive fix that stops the flake now — bounded exact-call recovery in the fixture for the documented fail-closed transient — rather than deferring all remediation to the next CI occurrence, since the named problem is that the fixture keeps blocking unrelated Verified votes.
evidence: Plan: 'so the NEXT CI occurrence pins the mechanism even if local reproduction fails'
Plan Context: 'it will keep blocking UNRELATED changes' Verified votes at random'
AC line 2: '_GitFailed now captures object-store forensics ... so the NEXT CI occurrence pins the deleter' — no fix that prevents recurrence
findings.finding: The plan lands instrumentation-only and explicitly defers the fix to a future CI occurrence, but the named problem is that the fixture 'will keep blocking UNRELATED changes' Verified votes at random.' Instrumentation makes the next failure legible but does not stop the flake, so the plan solves a proxy (diagnostic legibility) rather than the named problem (stop the intermittent ERROR).
scenarios: Between landing 1769 and the next organic occurrence, the fixture continues to ERROR intermittently and block unrelated Verified votes
findings.suggested_fix: Land the forensics AND a fixture-only bounded-retry wrapper (retry the raw resolver a few times, return on first complete map, raise loudly with the forensics after persistent failure) so unrelated changes stop being blocked while the deleter/transient is still being characterized.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider a fixture-robustness approach (bounded retry of the batched-map call, per the existing tests/_git_counts.py precedent) as the primary fix, because the resolver is documented fail-closed and the fixture's assumption that one raw call is non-empty is the changeable defect — this stops the flake where instrumentation only observes it.
evidence: Plan Scope names only 'env-scrubbed _git and/or maintenance.autoDetach=false' as candidate fixes — all object-store-directed
Final repair report (ticket): fix was '_fixture_batched_map performs at most five exact resolver attempts ... No src/rebar file changed', citing existing tests/_git_counts.py retry precedent
This alternative differs at the control-flow/interface boundary (fixture robustness vs object-store integrity) and is superior on fitness (stops the flake) and blast-radius (test-only, no src change)
findings.finding: The plan does not consider a structurally-different, clearly-superior alternative that was available from its own scope: treat the fixture's single-shot dependence on a fail-closed helper as the defect and add bounded exact-call recovery in the fixture (the repo already has transient-git-read retry infrastructure). This approach actually stops the flake and is the one that ultimately resolved the bug.
scenarios: Any transient git-read boundary in CI — the fixture recovers instead of ERRORing
